content:
The test image shows a green leaf with several small, discrete lesions scattered across the surface. Each lesion appears as a dark brown/necrotic spot with a lighter center, some appearing to have a shot-hole appearance (tissue falling out). The spots are circular to irregular, with dark brown margins.

**Key visual features:**
- Green leaf (mango-like, lanceolate)
- Multiple small brown necrotic spots with darker borders
- Some lesions appear sunken or with holes (shot-hole effect)
- Scattered distribution along the midrib and leaf surface
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No sooty black coating (rules out Sooty_Mould)
- No gall/swelling structures (rules out Gall_Midge)
- No stem dieback visible (rules out Die_Back)
- No obvious weevil cutting damage (rules out Cutting_Weevil)

**Candidates:**
- **Anthracnose**: Causes dark brown/black sunken lesions on leaves, often with necrotic centers — matches well
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Can cause water-soaked to necrotic spots with yellow halos on leaves

The lesions here are small, discrete, dark brown with somewhat defined margins and shot-hole appearance — this is very characteristic of **Anthracnose** on mango leaves (caused by *Colletotrichum gloeosporioides*). Bacterial canker typically shows more water-soaked margins or yellow halos. The dry, necrotic, well-defined spots without halo match anthracnose.
